name: Ehud Barak

summary.text: Ehud Barak (born 1942) is a former Israeli army chief of staff and politician. He was prime minister from 1999 to 2001 and served as deputy prime minister and defense minister from 2007 to 2013, leaving politics after announcing his retirement in November 2012. After leaving office he worked in business, including as chairman and investor in the emergency-communications startup Reporty (now Carbyne) through a 2015 limited partnership in which, Haaretz reported, Jeffrey Epstein supplied much of the money. In July 2019 he said he was seeking to remove the Epstein-linked firm from the partnership.

facts.claim: Barak served as Israel's prime minister from 1999 to 2001, having defeated Benjamin Netanyahu in the 1999 election, and left office in March 2001 after losing the February 2001 election for prime minister to Ariel Sharon.
facts.quote: the most highly decorated Israeli general, a former Chief of Staff and politician

facts.claim: In June 2007 Barak was elected leader of the Labor Party and was appointed deputy prime minister and minister of defense; he was reappointed to both posts in the Netanyahu government in March 2009, left Labor in January 2011 to form the Atzmaut party, and announced his retirement from politics in November 2012.
facts.quote: In June 2007, Ehud Barak was elected to head the Labor Party, and was subsequently appointed Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defense.

facts.claim: Haaretz reported in July 2019 that Barak formed an Israeli limited partnership in 2015, Sum (E.B.) 2015, to invest in Reporty (later Carbyne), and that a large part of the money the partnership used to buy Reporty stock was supplied by Jeffrey Epstein.
facts.quote: A large part of the money used by Sum to buy Reporty stock was supplied by Epstein, Haaretz reported Thursday.

facts.claim: In a July 2019 Facebook statement after Epstein's federal indictment, Barak said a firm linked to Epstein was a passive investor in his limited partnership and that he had instructed his attorneys to look into removing it.
facts.quote: he instructed his attorneys to look into removing the company tied to Epstein from the limited partnership once he heard of the indictment

facts.claim: In July 2019 the Daily Mail republished 2016 photographs of Barak entering Epstein's Manhattan home with his face partly covered. Barak threatened a libel suit, gave the paper a deadline to remove the article, and called the episode a 'blood libel'; the Daily Mail said it stood by its story and rejected the claim of political motives.
facts.quote: The UK newspaper ignored Barak's ultimatum that it remove the article from its website by 7pm Israel time or face a defamation suit.

facts.claim: Responding to the Daily Mail photographs on July 16, 2019, Barak wrote that he had been in Epstein's house but had never taken part in any party or meeting of the kind the article hinted at.
facts.quote: I indeed was in his house, I never took part in any party/meeting of the kind hinted to

facts.claim: Barak said he had visited Epstein's Manhattan homes and his Caribbean island but denied attending any sexual parties, The Times of Israel reported.
facts.quote: Barak says he visited Epstein at home, but didn't attend sex parties

facts.claim: After Justice Department documents released in 2026 showed that Barak and his wife stayed in regular contact with Epstein for years, including after Epstein's 2008 plea deal, Barak told Israel's N12 that he regretted the moment he met Epstein in 2003 and said he had cut ties in 2019 once the extent of Epstein's crimes came to light. He has acknowledged visiting Epstein numerous times, flying on his plane and staying at his New York apartment.
facts.quote: regrets the moment I met him in 2003
